sections.content:
Very interesting! After SPACE with white active on purple-over-white (50-50) from normal position:
- id=13: white, 100px, at [34,27] (single block again!)
- id=14: charcoal, 33px, at [63,0] (this is the HUD bar, not a lower block)
So SPACE with white active on purple-over-white (50-50) MERGED them back into a single white block! This makes sense because:
- When the active color matches one of the block colors, SPACE merges the blocks into a single block of that color
- Purple-over-white + SPACE white active → single white block (100px)
- Purple-over-white + SPACE purple active → single purple block (100px) (hypothetically)
So the SPACE mechanic is:
1. On a single block: splits into top=active, bottom=original (50-50)
2. On two same-color blocks: merges into one block
3. On two different-color blocks:
   - If active color matches one block: merges into that color
   - If active color matches neither: ??? (haven't tested)
So the cycle is:
- Single white → SPACE purple active → purple-over-white (50-50)
- Purple-over-white → SPACE white active → single white (100px)
- Purple-over-white → SPACE purple active → single purple (100px) (hypothetically)
But the goal is white-over-purple (50-50), not single white or purple-over-white. How do I get white-over-purple?
